title: Site configuration
description: The hand-written site.yaml that describes one site: identity, boundary, default view, and how the pipeline selects walkways.

id.description: Directory name under sites/ and the site segment of share URLs.

short_name.description: A brief name shown under the icon when the site is installed to a phone's home screen, where long names are cut off. Around 12 characters fit. Defaults to the name.

boundary.description: The area OpenStreetMap data is fetched for. Exactly one of the three forms.

view.description: Where the map opens before a position is known.

units.description: How distances are shown: metres and kilometres, or feet and miles.

categories.description: The kinds of place this site has, in the order the map legend lists them, each with the name people read. A kind's position in the list also decides its colour on the map. Kinds the site's places use but this list leaves out are added after it, named from their value.

id.description: The category value places carry, such as call_box.

label.description: The name shown in the legend, such as Call boxes.

nearest.description: Place categories that get a one-tap "nearest" button. Each entry names a category used by this site's places and the label its button shows. Nearest is measured by walking distance over the network, not straight-line.

category.description: A category value as used in places.yaml.

label.description: The word shown on the button and read to a screen reader, for example "Parking" or "Call box".

walkways.description: Which OpenStreetMap highway values count as walkways for this site.

unpaved.description: Surface values that make a way unusable here, replacing the default list.

max_connector_m.description: A place whose entrance is further than this from a walkway is reported.

snap_m.description: How far a hand-drawn walkway's end may be from a mapped walkway and still be joined to it.

join_crossings.description: Whether walkways that cross at ground level without sharing a point are joined where they cross. OpenStreetMap treats such a crossing as unconnected, which is right for a bridge and usually an omission elsewhere; ways tagged as a bridge, a tunnel, or on another layer are never joined. Off by default.

parking_aisles.description: Whether the aisles of parking lots count as walkways. On by default: people walk through lots, and the router can still prefer sidewalks.

roads.description: Highway values of roads a pedestrian may walk along when nothing better exists; they join sidewalks and parking aisles into one network. Replaces the default list.

routing.description: How the router weighs the network. Omitted values take the defaults given here.

weights.description: Cost multiplier per edge kind: a route's cost is metres times the kind's weight, so a weight of 3 makes a road worth walking only when every alternative is more than three times longer. Weights are at least 1.

walking_speed.description: Metres per second, used for the time estimate shown with a route.

tiles.description: Where the site's base map tiles are extracted from. The pipeline's tiles command reads only the tiles covering the site's data, plus a margin and, at the zoom levels the map can show, a ring of neighbouring tiles, from a planet-wide PMTiles archive and writes basemap.pmtiles into the site directory.

source.description: URL of a PMTiles archive that answers HTTP range requests, for example a dated Protomaps basemap build.

margin_m.description: How far beyond the site's walkways and places the extract reaches, in metres.

max_zoom.description: Highest zoom level to extract; the source's own maximum when omitted. The map overzooms beyond it.

overlays.description: Images of the site's own maps, georeferenced by control points: a pixel in the image paired with the OpenStreetMap element or the position it depicts.

image.description: PNG file, relative to the site directory.

pixel.description: Column then row, from the top-left corner of the image.

position.description: Longitude then latitude, as GeoJSON orders them.

bbox.description: South, west, north, east in degrees, the order Overpass uses.
